taxonomic_note: Kew/POWO accepted name used canonically. Some regional sources show an expanded author citation; the taxon concept is the same.
look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: typically ONE to THREE curved combs or 'eyebrows' clustered at the TOP of the flowering stem, with many closely packed spikelets all the way to the raceme tip. Blue grama normally does NOT leave a long naked pointed tip beyond the final spikelet; compare with hairy grama's stinger.
project_tracker_diagnostic: perennial tufted/caespitose warm-season grass with short stout rhizomes; leaves concentrated mainly near the base; usually 1–3 conspicuous curved unilateral pectinate racemes; racemes about 1.5–5 cm long and spreading to arcuate; many crowded spikelets continue to the end of the raceme; no long naked rachis tip or 'stinger' beyond the spikelets

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Beautiful Hays County documents volunteer Bouteloua gracilis thriving on an unmanaged dry slope and treats it within the local native-grass context; BONAP is retained as the primary native-range authority. Uvalde — Texas A&M/OakTrust Uvalde vascular-plant survey records Bouteloua gracilis collected in Uvalde (collection 824, 25 Oct 2002). Crockett — USDA-NRCS Plant Materials Center blue grama evaluation lists accession 9093104 with origin Crockett County, Texas.

crew_field_steps: Count the conspicuous curved eyebrows on ONE flowering stem, avoiding nearby stems behind the subject.
Follow an individual comb from stem attachment along its packed spikelets to the end; look for a naked extended rachis tip or lack thereof.
Against hairy grama's bristly branch with exposed projecting tip and Texas grama's numerous short fuzzy heads, use close seedhead architecture; not purple color.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Complete erect flowering stem with count of terminal branches and visible base.
Same-scale exact-blue comb showing tip, spikelet arrangement, and whether rachis extends bare.
Flowering details with anthers (not confused with spikelets).
Leaf sheath/ligule; compare with B. hirsuta and B. rigidiseta.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Blue grama usually bears 1–3 long curved terminal eyebrow combs whose spikelets extend nearly to the end. Hairy grama often has dense long hairs and a conspicuously bare terminal rachis projection. Pectinata is generally taller with longer and often more numerous combs but overlaps hairy. Texas grama has several much shorter bristly clustered branches. Sideoats has many short side branches all the way down a long stem.
